destination.name: Narooma
destination.tagline: Far South Coast fishing town, boat base for the seals of Montague Island.
destination.description: Narooma is a town of about 8,500 on the Princes Highway, where Wagonga Inlet meets the ocean. Barunguba Montague Island, a short boat trip offshore, has hundreds of seals and more than 90 bird species, and Wikivoyage notes the largest penguin colony in NSW. Around the town, the heritage village of Central Tilba, Bermagui's rock pool and surf beaches, and Eurobodalla National Park fill out a longer stay.
whyVisit: Swim in Blue Pool at Bermagui
Camp and surf in Eurobodalla National Park

goodToKnow.title: Montague Island is boat-only
goodToKnow.detail: Tours depend on weather and run about $100–165; the reserve is closed during August. Seals are best seen from late winter to early December.

goodToKnow.title: Tilba shops keep short hours
goodToKnow.detail: Central Tilba is easily covered on foot, with shops open roughly 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Bar crossing is hazardous
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage warns the bar at Narooma is the most dangerous boat crossing in NSW; skippers must call Coastal Patrol first.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} suit Montague Island seals, birds and passing whales, then summer beach weather.
